answer: Each agent’s voting weight can be tied to a scarce, nontransferable deposit locked for a fixed horizon, with votes counted only after the deposit has aged and the agent has completed randomly sampled, verifiable tasks. Splitting one identity into many does not create more weight: the attacker must lock additional capital for each agent and risk losing it when sampled work fails. An atlas of task records can make audits reproducible, while a lotus-style recovery process can preserve legitimate agents’ history without letting them duplicate their deposit.
